review: ISSUES:
- (miscited) "a small, hydraulically active volume of macropores and cracks delivers particulate phosphorus and sediment to drains within hours, so tiles frequently dominate edge-of-field phosphorus loads \parencite{Williams2018,King2014}" -- the source attributes this preferential-flow/particulate-P and "tiles frequently dominate edge-of-field phosphorus loads" claim to \parencite{Pease2018} (intro) and \parencite{Pease2018,Sharpley1995} (conclusions). In the source, King2014 and Williams2018 are used only for streamflow fraction / field water export (\parencite{King2014,Williams2018,Schilling2019}), not for the phosphorus preferential-flow claim, so these are swapped keys.
- (miscited) "cover crops clustering around $40$--$60\%$ nitrate-load reduction, alongside controlled drainage, bioreactors, wetlands, and saturated buffers governed by residence time, temperature, and loading---so meeting downstream targets requires stacking complementary measures \parencite{Smith2011,Gowda2012}" -- the source attributes the 40--60% cover-crop reduction to \parencite{Malone2018,Malone2014b,Malone2023} and the edge-of-field residence-time/temperature/loading controls to \parencite{Christianson2013,Jaynes2008}. Smith2011 and Gowda2012 appear in the source only for the modeling/geophysics/remote-sensing toolkit (\parencite{Smith2011,Singh2019b,Gowda2012,Allred2020}), not for mitigation practices, so these keys are swapped.
